## Transfer with a Russian-speaking guide on Easter Island

[Easter Island, or Rapa Nui](/chile/place/easter-island/), is far from mainland Chile. After the flight, it is especially convenient to be able to discuss travel arrangements in a familiar language. We offer **a transfer with a Russian-speaking guide**: a journey during which you can agree on the first steps on the island and discuss your subsequent sightseeing plans.

This is an important distinction from a full sightseeing tour. The word "transfer" primarily refers to transport arrangements. Detailed archaeological visits, stops at individual moai sites and national park admission tickets are not listed among the services included with this transfer.

## What makes Rapa Nui special

The island is known for its Polynesian culture, volcanic landscapes and stone statues called **moai**. Many stand on ceremonial platforms known as *ahu*. Rapa Nui National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and the island's archaeological heritage is significant worldwide.

Its main settlement is **Hanga Roa**, where many hotels, restaurants and traveler services are located. The first steps on the island therefore usually concern practical matters around the town: checking in, planning the following days, communicating and arranging transport.

A transfer provides an initial orientation. However, **having a Russian-speaking escort does not automatically turn the journey into a guided tour of all the historic sites**.

## Practical matters to settle at the start of the trip

On arrival, it is useful to confirm the accommodation address and arrangements for subsequent outings, local travel distances, departure times for archaeological visits and the rules for accessing those sites. Communication in Russian helps reduce misunderstandings, especially for visitors who do not speak Spanish.

Rapa Nui differs from Chile's major cities in its remoteness from the mainland and the small scale of its settlements. It is sensible to plan the order of nature and cultural excursions in advance while leaving time to rest after the flight.

The precise **meeting point, end point of the transfer, vehicle model and journey time** are not specified in this transfer's terms. They must be confirmed when booking rather than inferred from general information about Hanga Roa.

## How a transfer differs from a moai excursion

The moai are Rapa Nui's best-known cultural symbol. Visiting them, however, involves particular archaeological sites, national park regulations, time for stops and a guide following a separate itinerary.

| Service | What is confirmed |
|---|---|
| Transfer with a Russian-speaking guide | Transport and communication in Russian |
| Moai excursion | A separate itinerary visiting archaeological sites |

If your objective is to see the famous groups of statues, volcanic craters and ceremonial platforms, choose a cultural excursion that includes them. Do not try to fit the entire island's archaeological heritage into a short transfer.

You can compare options in the [Easter Island excursion catalog](/chile/easter-island/) and on the [Rapa Nui destination page](/chile/place/easter-island/).

## Preparing for arrival

Before traveling, keep your accommodation booking details, the meeting representative's contact information and the confirmed meeting point readily available. Given the island's isolation, agreeing on the first few hours in advance is especially helpful, rather than resolving every arrangement after landing.

Entry requirements for Rapa Nui, permitted length of stay, required documents and national park access rules should be checked against Chile's current official requirements for the traveler's citizenship. Booking this transfer does not replace compliance with those rules.

The island can be windy and experience tropical showers, so lightweight rain protection and comfortable footwear are useful even on arrival day.

## Ada Tours pricing and terms

**The transfer costs $83 per person.** Discounts may be available when booking for several travelers; specific conditions are discussed separately.

**Russian-language assistance** is provided during the transfer. Admission tickets, meals and paid excursions are not separately listed as inclusions. It is therefore best to confirm the scope of the service, the meeting point and the destination in advance, and book archaeological visits under their own programs.

If Rapa Nui forms part of a longer journey, explore [tours of Chile](/chile/tour/) early to understand how many days you will actually have on the island.

## Frequently asked questions about the Rapa Nui transfer

### How much does the transfer cost?

**$83 per person.** Discounts may be offered for several travelers.

### Does the escort speak Russian?

Yes. Russian is specified as the language in the published service description.

### Does it include visiting the moai?

There is no confirmed list of archaeological visits: this is a transfer, not a full island tour.

### Where are travelers met?

The exact meeting point and destination address are agreed when booking.

## Easter Island excursions: routes to the moai, volcanoes and Anakena

[Easter Island, or Rapa Nui](/chile/place/easter-island/), is best explored through several themed excursions. Ceremonial moai platforms, ancient quarries, craters and coastal monuments lie in different parts of the island. A single overview trip is not enough to see all of them in depth.

We offer excursions along the **south coast**, routes to **Ahu Akivi and Puna Pau**, a separate visit to **Orongo and Rano Kau**, and a [transfer with a Russian-speaking guide](/chile/easter-island/easter-island-transfer-russian-speaking-guide/). The latter is a transport service for the start of a journey and should not be treated as a substitute for an archaeological excursion.

## Three excursion areas: which to choose first

| Route | Main highlight |
|---|---|
| South coast | Moai, Rano Raraku, Anakena |
| Ahu Akivi and Puna Pau | Seven moai, red tuff |
| Orongo and Rano Kau | Crater and the birdman tradition |

**The south coast** is the richest archaeological route, including [Ahu Akahanga](/chile/place/ahu-akahanga/) with its fallen figures, [Rano Raraku](/chile/place/rano-raraku-volcano/) where statues were carved, [Ahu Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/) with 15 restored moai, and [Anakena Beach](/chile/place/anakena-beach/). You can choose the ["Anakena, Rano Raraku and Tongariki" route](/chile/easter-island/anakena-rano-raraku-tongariki-tour/) or a [private south-coast excursion](/chile/easter-island/south-coast-moai-anakena-private/). Another itinerary includes a [private picnic on Anakena](/chile/easter-island/easter-island-south-coast-anakena-private-picnic/).

**The central and western monuments** are best explored on routes to [Ahu Akivi](/chile/place/ahu-akivi/), the [Puna Pau quarry](/chile/place/puna-pau-quarry/) and [Tahai](/chile/place/tahai/). Seven moai stand at Ahu Akivi; Puna Pau supplied the red stone used for the statues' pukao topknots. The basic ["Ahu Akivi and Puna Pau" excursion](/chile/easter-island/ahu-akivi-puna-pau-tour/) takes about four hours. Longer versions include Tahai and other stops.

**[Orongo and Rano Kau](/chile/easter-island/orongo-rano-kau-tour/)** reveal a different aspect of Rapa Nui's culture. The [Rano Kau volcano](/chile/place/rano-kau-volcano/) is known for its large crater, while the ceremonial [village of Orongo](/chile/place/orongo-village/) is connected to the Tangata Manu, or birdman, tradition. We allocate about four hours to this route.

## How the south-coast excursions differ

Three products share famous landmarks, but their contents are different.

- ["Anakena, Rano Raraku and Ahu Tongariki"](/chile/easter-island/anakena-rano-raraku-tongariki-tour/) visits Akahanga, Rano Raraku, Tongariki, the Poike area and Anakena; a packed lunch is explicitly listed.
- ["Easter Island South Coast and Anakena Beach"](/chile/easter-island/south-coast-moai-anakena-private/) is a private excursion with an English-speaking guide and boxed lunch; it also includes Ahu Vaihu and Ahu Nau Nau.
- ["Easter Island: South Coast and Private Picnic on Anakena"](/chile/easter-island/easter-island-south-coast-anakena-private-picnic/) emphasizes a private picnic by the shore after the archaeological stops.

Your choice depends on the guiding arrangements, meals and how much time you want by the sea. You can compare the Akahanga stop in particular in the [excursion catalog for Ahu Akahanga](/chile/ahu-akahanga/). **Do not assume that the included services of one itinerary apply to another just because they visit the same monuments.**

## Ahu Akivi, Puna Pau and Tahai: similar names, different programs

We offer several cultural itineraries through the island's central area. The [short Ahu Akivi and Puna Pau excursion](/chile/easter-island/ahu-akivi-puna-pau-tour/) focuses on two sites. The [private "Ahu Akivi, Puna Pau and Tahai" program](/chile/easter-island/easter-island-akivi-puna-pau-tahai/) adds the coastal Tahai complex.

["Ahu Akivi, Hanga Pukure, Puna Pau and Tahai"](/chile/easter-island/akivi-hanga-pukure-puna-pau-tahai-private/) also includes the unrestored Hanga Pukure platform. This product specifies four hours and an English-speaking guide, with Russian-language guiding available at extra cost. Another [Ahu Akivi, Puna Pau and Tahai itinerary](/chile/easter-island/easter-island-akivi-puna-pau-tahai-visit/) mentions Hanga Pukure as well, but its commercial terms must be compared using its own product page.

Similar lists of places are a reason to compare the **actual route, format and guide services**, not proof that the products are identical. Separate terms and itineraries should not be combined into one imaginary package.

## How many days to set aside for excursions

To cover Rapa Nui's main stories, plan for **several full sightseeing days**: one for the south coast, another for the central monuments, and a third day or half-day for Orongo and Rano Kau. This is planning guidance, not a fixed duration for every available tour.

The longer southern routes have many stops. If archaeological explanations and photography matter to you, avoid crowding the schedule with unnecessary additional sites. Island weather can affect the condition of paths and access to particular places; free time between excursions makes it easier to adjust a day's plans calmly.

A separate [transfer with a Russian-speaking guide](/chile/easter-island/easter-island-transfer-russian-speaking-guide/) is available for arrival, check-in and an introduction to local logistics. Its published price applies only to the transfer, not to every excursion listed here.

## Tickets, guides and national park rules

Rapa Nui's monuments are protected and visits are regulated by park authorities. Travelers need to consider admission tickets, accredited guides and current restrictions on access to individual sites. Rules may vary from one site to another, so establish exactly what is included in the excursion you purchase.

At archaeological sites, visitors must not touch statues or platforms, collect stones or leave marked trails. A well-planned route allows time to learn about each monument and view it respectfully without approaching fragile features.

Do not assume Russian-speaking assistance is provided on every excursion: some product descriptions explicitly specify English, while others do not state a language. When choosing, clarify which arrangements require a separate Russian-speaking guide.

## Frequently asked questions about Easter Island excursions

### What should I see on my first Easter Island excursion?

For an introduction, travelers often choose the [south coast with Rano Raraku, Tongariki and Anakena](/chile/easter-island/anakena-rano-raraku-tongariki-tour/). It brings together several important chapters in the history of the moai.

### Are there excursions lasting about four hours?

Yes. About four hours is specified for [Ahu Akivi and Puna Pau](/chile/easter-island/ahu-akivi-puna-pau-tour/) and [Orongo and Rano Kau](/chile/easter-island/orongo-rano-kau-tour/). A separate private itinerary including Hanga Pukure also lists four hours.

### Can I book a private itinerary?

Yes. Options include a [private south-coast excursion](/chile/easter-island/south-coast-moai-anakena-private/) and a [private Ahu Akivi itinerary including Hanga Pukure](/chile/easter-island/akivi-hanga-pukure-puna-pau-tahai-private/). Check the included services for each one.

### Do all excursions include national park admission?

There is no single confirmation that park admission is included in all excursions. Consult the inclusion list for the individual program and the current park access rules.

### Does the transfer with a Russian-speaking guide include moai excursions?

No. The [transfer with a Russian-speaking guide](/chile/easter-island/easter-island-transfer-russian-speaking-guide/) is a separate product. Archaeological routes are selected and agreed independently.

## Orongo and Rano Kau volcano: sacred places on Easter Island

On [Easter Island, or Rapa Nui](/chile/place/easter-island/), the landscape of [Rano Kau volcano](/chile/place/rano-kau-volcano/) and the ceremonial [village of Orongo](/chile/place/orongo-village/) offer an insight into the island's Polynesian heritage beyond its famous stone moai statues.

The Ada Tours excursion lasts **about four hours**. It begins on the slopes of Rano Kau, continues to a viewpoint overlooking the crater and then visits Orongo. Here, guests learn about **Tangata Manu**, the birdman tradition that played a significant role in Rapa Nui's social and ritual life.

## Rano Kau: a crater with a lake inside the volcano

[Rano Kau](/chile/place/rano-kau-volcano/) lies in the southwestern part of Easter Island. It is a volcanic massif with a large crater containing a lake. From an elevated viewpoint, visitors see an extraordinary landscape: slopes surround the water, with the Pacific Ocean stretching beyond the outer rim.

The crater matters for more than geology. The island's volcanic history shaped its coastline and high slopes, and its natural environment influenced the lives of local people. Rano Kau shows that Rapa Nui is a volcanic island where cultural heritage is closely connected to distinctive landforms.

The weather can change quickly. Clouds may partly obscure the crater, while strong winds are common in exposed areas. A viewpoint stop does not mean visitors can walk freely along dangerous crater edges: the guide's instructions and protected-area restrictions must be followed.

## Orongo: Rapa Nui's ceremonial village

After Rano Kau, the excursion continues to [Orongo](/chile/place/orongo-village/), a ceremonial settlement on the edge of the volcanic massif. Stone structures associated with the island's rituals survive here.

UNESCO identifies Orongo as one of the most distinctive sites associated with the birdman tradition. The settlement includes semi-subterranean stone buildings and petroglyphs expressing ideas about the surrounding world, rituals and social organization.

These structures are unusual in both form and setting. Their meaning becomes much clearer when explained in the context of Rapa Nui traditions: simply walking among the stone walls without historical commentary reveals far less about the place.

## The Tangata Manu ritual: what the birdman means

The **Tangata Manu** tradition was linked to an annual contest between clan representatives and the retrieval of the season's first egg from the manutara seabird. According to historical accounts, competitors had to reach an offshore islet, locate the first egg and bring it back according to the ritual's rules.

Victory had political and ritual significance for the group represented by the competitor. The tradition became an important form of social organization on the island after earlier religious practices changed.

Today, this is **historical heritage**, not an event staged for tourists. The excursion explains the places and context of the ritual; it does not include participating in the contest or visiting the remote islets where it took place.

## Motu Nui: the islet connected to Orongo's history

The ceremonial village overlooks small offshore islets. One of them, **Motu Nui**, is especially important for understanding the Tangata Manu tradition.

Competitors in the historic ritual tried to reach the seabirds' nesting grounds. Their route involved difficult coastal terrain and the ocean. On the modern excursion, these circumstances are explained from Orongo's viewpoints: **landing on Motu Nui is not included in our program**.

The views also show how geography shaped a cultural practice. The cliffs, height and remoteness of the islets formed part of the contest's challenges and help explain its symbolic significance.

## How Orongo differs from moai excursions

The famous moai are stone statues created by the people of Rapa Nui and erected on ceremonial platforms called ahu. [Easter Island](/chile/place/easter-island/) is renowned for them, but they represent only part of the island's cultural history.

Visiting Orongo reveals **a different tradition**, associated with the birdman. It therefore complements visits to statue complexes, particularly when an island itinerary spans more than one day.

| Moai and ahu | Orongo and Rano Kau |
|---|---|
| Stone statues | Ceremonial village |
| Ancestor worship | Tangata Manu |
| Platforms around the island | Crater and coastal views |

Seeing moai in photographs of the island does not mean a particular statue platform is included in the Rano Kau and Orongo excursion. They are separate stops, and the list of visited sites should be agreed in advance.

## Tips for the four-hour excursion

Comfortable non-slip footwear, a windproof jacket and sun protection are useful at exposed viewpoints. Volcanic terrain can be uneven, and reaching certain viewpoints may require care.

At protected monuments, visitors must stay on permitted paths, avoid touching petroglyphs and refrain from moving stones. These rules help preserve the heritage of Rapa Nui's Indigenous people.

A duration of about **four hours** makes this a half-day outing. However, the exact transfer times, guiding language and admission arrangements must be confirmed for the selected program, as they are not specified in our excursion's terms.

## Frequently asked questions about Orongo and Rano Kau

### How long is the excursion?

About **four hours**, including visits to the crater and the ceremonial village.

### Can we see the lake inside Rano Kau's crater?

Yes. The route includes a viewpoint, although visibility depends on the weather.

### Is the birdman ritual still performed for tourists?

No. The excursion introduces the historical Tangata Manu tradition and its monuments; it does not involve participating in the old ritual.

### Can we land on Motu Nui?

Landing on Motu Nui is not part of this itinerary. The islet is discussed in its historical context.

## Tours featuring Rano Kau and Orongo: choosing an Easter Island itinerary

[Rano Kau volcano](/chile/place/rano-kau-volcano/) and the [village of Orongo](/chile/place/orongo-village/) reveal aspects of Rapa Nui's history beyond its famous rows of moai. The ceremonial landscape survives here, linked to the Tangata Manu birdman tradition. Unlike the quarries where statues were carved, the story of Orongo concerns later rituals, clans and competitions.

The [stand-alone "Orongo and Rano Kau Volcano" excursion](/chile/easter-island/orongo-rano-kau-tour/) lasts **around four hours**. This collection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} that incorporate the excursion into longer itineraries. The main decision is how many days to devote to the island itself and what other experiences come before and after Orongo.

## What the excursion covers

The first part of the route follows the slopes of [Rano Kau](/chile/place/rano-kau-volcano/). From a viewpoint, visitors can see the crater and the lake within it. This introduction to the island's volcanic landscape helps explain why a ceremonial settlement developed in such a striking natural location.

Next is [Orongo](/chile/place/orongo-village/). The archaeological complex lies near the crater rim, overlooking small offshore islets. In its stone structures, participants in the traditional ritual awaited the arrival of the manutara bird. The excursion explains the clan representatives' contest for the bird's first egg and the selection of the Tangata Manu.

Chile's National Cultural Heritage Service recognizes Orongo as one of the island's most important monuments. Surviving semi-subterranean stone houses and petroglyphs make it especially valuable. Viewpoints and archaeological structures form a continuous cultural route, so allow time to explore rather than making only a brief photo stop.

## Three-day island tour or a longer South American journey

**["Easter Island: Three Days Among Moai and Volcanoes"](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/).** In this stand-alone three-day itinerary, Rano Kau and Orongo are scheduled for **day one**. Day two covers the south-coast monuments, [Rano Raraku](/chile/place/rano-raraku-volcano/), [Ahu Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/) and [Anakena](/chile/place/anakena-beach/); day three focuses on western archaeological sites. This option suits travelers whose main goal is Rapa Nui.

**["Chile and Argentina: 17-Day Grand Tour with Iguazu"](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/).** The volcano and Orongo are visited on **day three**, after arrival on the island. The next day is devoted to the coast, moai and Anakena, followed by an Ahu Akivi excursion and a return to Santiago. Here Rapa Nui is part of a larger journey including the Atacama, Patagonia, the Mendoza wine region, Iguazu and Buenos Aires. It is a multi-stage trip involving several flights.

**["VIP: 33-Day Grand Tour of South America"](/multi-country/tour/south-america-luxury-33-days/).** In this itinerary, the flight to the island, transfer and visit to Rano Kau and Orongo are scheduled for **day 22**. A separate day then covers coastal monuments and Anakena. The island is just one part of a route through Peru, Bolivia and Chile, so the timing and physical demands must be considered across the whole program rather than one excursion.

Orongo is also linked to a [14-day Peru, Bolivia and Chile itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-peru-bolivia-chile-easter-island/). For this tour, it is particularly important to clarify the actual order of the island section relative to the mainland program. The presence of an excursion link does not mean all the stops can fit into a single day.

| Format | What it offers |
|---|---|
| 3 days on the island | A focus on Rapa Nui |
| 17-day grand tour | The island plus Chile and Argentina |
| 33-day journey | The island within a long expedition |

## How Orongo fits with the moai monuments

To understand the island, it helps to distinguish three groups of sites. [Rano Raraku](/chile/place/rano-raraku-volcano/) is the quarry where moai were carved. [Ahu Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/) is an immense ceremonial platform with 15 restored statues. [Orongo](/chile/place/orongo-village/) is associated with the birdman tradition, which reflects changes in the island's culture.

Visiting Orongo therefore does not replace a full day at [Rano Raraku and Anakena](/chile/easter-island/anakena-rano-raraku-tongariki-tour/). These sites are visited on different days in the three-day island program. The same principle applies to longer journeys: the history of the moai and that of Tangata Manu are explored on separate excursions.

To learn about the island's western sites, consider adding [Ahu Akivi, Puna Pau and Tahai](/chile/easter-island/easter-island-akivi-puna-pau-tahai/), where you can discover the seven moai, the red tuff used for their topknots and restored ceremonial platforms.

## Restrictions to check in advance

Rapa Nui National Park requires a separate admission ticket and an accredited guide. Under the published rules, **Orongo may be visited once per ticket**, as may Rano Raraku. When planning several days on the island, these visits should be allocated in advance. At archaeological sites, visitors must stay on designated routes and must not touch moai or petroglyphs.

There is also a separate entry process for the island in addition to the general requirements for mainland Chile. Chilean authorities require tourists to complete an advance registration form, provide proof of accommodation at a registered property and hold a return ticket. The applicability and current procedures must be checked for each traveler before booking.

Rano Kau is in an exposed, windy landscape. Walking sections call for comfortable non-slip footwear and protection from sun and wind. If the visit falls on arrival day, check actual flight times and the time needed for the transfer. In the 17-day and 33-day itineraries, the island day includes other transport arrangements, so allowing extra time matters.

## Which tour featuring Orongo should you choose?

If Rapa Nui's archaeology and natural landscapes are your main interests, compare the [three-day Easter Island program](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/) with the option of allocating more days to visits. For a much broader journey, the [17-day grand tour](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/) and [33-day VIP itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-luxury-33-days/) cover more destinations but also involve more transfers.

You can also explore [all Chile tours](/chile/tour/), [cultural and historical itineraries in Chile](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/chile/) and the [Easter Island destination page](/chile/place/easter-island/). These programs vary in duration, visited sites and the role of Rapa Nui within the overall journey.

## Frequently asked questions about tours featuring Orongo and Rano Kau

### How long does a visit to Rano Kau and Orongo take?

According to Ada Tours' stand-alone excursion, it takes **about four hours**. On a longer tour, timing may depend on flight arrival, transfers and the day's overall itinerary.

### Is Orongo where the moai were carved?

No. [Orongo](/chile/place/orongo-village/) is a ceremonial settlement linked to Tangata Manu. The statue quarry is at [Rano Raraku](/chile/place/rano-raraku-volcano/).

### Can Orongo be visited twice on the same ticket?

Under national park rules, **no**: one visit to Orongo is permitted on a single admission ticket. A repeat visit requires separate arrangements and compliance with the applicable access rules.

### How many days should I spend on Easter Island?

For the main monuments, we offer a [three-day program](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/). Travelers who prefer to explore at a slower pace can discuss a longer stay and allow time for flights.

## Easter Island's south coast: moai, Rano Raraku and Anakena Beach

[Easter Island, or Rapa Nui](/chile/place/easter-island/), is famous for its stone moai, but their story comes into focus when you visit different parts of the island. Some platforms hold fallen statues, while others display restored monuments. The quarry reveals how statues were carved, and coastal sites help explain why ceremonial structures stood in particular locations.

Our **full-day private excursion** covers south-coast monuments, [Rano Raraku](/chile/place/rano-raraku-volcano/), [Ahu Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/) and [Anakena Beach](/chile/place/anakena-beach/). **An English-speaking guide and packed lunch are included.** A Russian-speaking guide can be arranged for an additional charge. The route ends back at the hotel in [Hanga Roa](/chile/place/hanga-roa/).

## Ahu Vaihu and Ahu Akahanga: monuments in their historical condition

The excursion begins along the south coast. At [Ahu Vaihu](/chile/place/ahu-vaihu/), in Hanga Te'e Bay, visitors can examine an unrestored ceremonial platform. The fallen moai offer a glimpse of the monuments' history before modern restoration efforts.

[Ahu Akahanga](/chile/place/ahu-akahanga/) is also an important historical site. Local tradition associates it with the burial of the first ruler, Hotu Matu'a. This account belongs to oral tradition, and it is useful to distinguish the legend from archaeological evidence.

Both stops provide context for the next part of the trip. After ruined and collapsed platforms, restored Ahu Tongariki makes a very different impression. Visitors should never touch the stone monuments or enter restricted areas for a photograph.

## Rano Raraku: where the moai were carved

[Rano Raraku](/chile/place/rano-raraku-volcano/) is the volcanic quarry where most of the island's moai were carved. Statues at different stages of production remain on its slopes: some stand or are partly embedded in the ground, while others remain close to where they were made.

This is one of the route's most informative stops. You can imagine the work of the sculptors separating large figures from volcanic tuff. According to UNESCO, there are approximately **900 moai** across Rapa Nui, and the quarries are vital evidence of how they were made.

A **packed lunch outdoors** is included in the excursion. The inclusion is confirmed, although the exact menu is not specified. While walking, follow national park rules and protect the archaeological sites.

## Ahu Tongariki: 15 restored statues

The next stop is [Ahu Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/), the island's largest ceremonial platform. It holds **15 restored moai**. The row of statues allows visitors to compare their sizes and understand how the monuments were positioned in relation to the ahu.

An ahu is a distinctive type of ceremonial platform in Rapa Nui culture. UNESCO recognizes these structures and sculptures as outstanding Polynesian cultural heritage. Both the statues themselves and the human-built stone platform beneath them are important.

The route then continues to [Ahu Te Pito Kura](/chile/place/ahu-te-pito-kura/), with the well-known stone called the "Navel of the World." Local beliefs are best understood as part of the island's traditions rather than confused with archaeologically established dates.

## Anakena: a sandy beach and Ahu Nau Nau

At [Anakena Beach](/chile/place/anakena-beach/), white sand and palms stand beside [Ahu Nau Nau](/chile/place/ahu-nau-nau/). It is an especially unusual place to experience Rapa Nui, where swimming and beach time take place close to an archaeological monument.

There will be **time for a walk and a swim**. Whether entering the water is suitable on a particular date depends on the weather, waves and local beach guidance. Swimwear, a towel and sun protection will be useful.

After Anakena, the journey crosses the island's interior to return to Hanga Roa. In a single day, travelers see several stages in the monuments' lives rather than just one statue: carving at the quarry, ceremonial platforms, destruction and restoration.

## Preparing for the excursion

A long day calls for comfortable closed-toe shoes, a hat, drinking water and lightweight protection from wind and sun. Some stops are in open areas without shelter from rain or strong sunshine. Bring swimming essentials for Anakena.

Access to individual archaeological sites is governed by Rapa Nui National Park rules. Admission procedures and any required guiding arrangements are checked when organizing the excursion; the monuments cannot all be visited freely without restrictions.

If you have less time on the island, compare this excursion with the [four-hour route via Ahu Akivi, Puna Pau and Tahai](/chile/easter-island/akivi-hanga-pukure-puna-pau-tahai-private/). It visits different sites and does not replace the longer journey to Rano Raraku and Anakena.

## Frequently asked questions about the south-coast excursion

### Will we visit Ahu Tongariki and the Rano Raraku quarry in one day?

Yes. Both are part of this **full-day itinerary**, along with south-coast platforms and a stop at Anakena.

### Is lunch included, and what language does the guide speak?

**A packed lunch and an English-speaking guide are included.** Russian-language guiding can be arranged at additional cost.

### Is there time to swim at Anakena?

Yes. The itinerary provides time for swimming and walking. Actual water conditions depend on the weather and local safety rules.
